name: Dubrovnik
dek: DHMZ's 1971–2000 atlas sheet for Dubrovnik. The 1991–2020 NCEI submission does not have this station.
paragraphs: Croatia's NOAA submission has Zagreb-Maksimir and Split-Marjan and does not have Dubrovnik. The table is the DHMZ climate-atlas sheet labelled Dubrovnik for 1971–2000. The figures are the lowercase average daily maximum, the lowercase average daily minimum, and precipitation. The same PDF prints a 1961–1990 block. It was not averaged in. The city page on meteo.hr is labelled 1961–2024 and gives a mean and absolute extremes, which are not an average daily high and low.
The atlas sheet does not print a height or a WMO number, so those cells are empty. The plug, the road rule, the tipping note, and the ministry link are the national ones.

climate.caption: Station sheet: Dubrovnik, in the DHMZ climate atlas. Period printed on the sheet: 1971–2000. Not a 1991–2020 normal.
climate.note: The Croatian submission in the NOAA NCEI 1991–2020 collection has Zagreb-Maksimir and Split-Marjan and does not have Dubrovnik. This table is the DHMZ climate-atlas sheet labelled Dubrovnik for 1971–2000. The rows used are the lowercase tmax and tmin under air temperature, which are the average daily maximum and minimum, and precipitation R. Uppercase Tmax and Tmin on the same sheet are the absolute extremes and are not printed here. The same PDF also prints 1961–1990. Those rows were not averaged with 1971–2000. The live DHMZ city page is labelled 1961–2024 and gives a mean, an absolute maximum, and an absolute minimum. It does not give an average daily high and low, so it is not this table. The atlas sheet does not print a height or a WMO number.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type C and F, 230 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows Croatia at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page on 15 November 2026 did not return the list. The archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Article 47(1) of the Road Traffic Safety Act, in the consolidation on zakon.hr, says a vehicle moves on the right side of the carriageway. The page lists the amendments through Narodne novine 145/24 and says the text is in force from 21 December 2024. The site is a consolidation. The official gazette text of each amendment was not opened separately.
driving.sourceTitle: Zakon o sigurnosti prometa na cestama, članak 47, zakon.hr

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.value: Not mandatory; 10–15% in a restaurant if you do
tipping.detail: The Croatia.hr tipping page says a tip is a sign of respect and is considered a tradition, and that it is not mandatory. It says that if you are happy with the service, smaller café and bar bills are rounded up at least to the next whole number, and larger amounts or restaurant bills get a tip of at least 10 to 15 percent of the total. No date is printed on the page.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Croatia, last reviewed 25 August 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Euro and the code EUR for Croatia. The list's published date, in the Pblshd attribute, is 17 September 2026.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab names Croatia Europe/Zagreb. zone1970.tab puts Croatia on one row with Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Slovenia, and the zone name on that row is Europe/Belgrade. The backward file links Europe/Zagreb to Europe/Belgrade. This sheet prints Europe/Zagreb, which is the name zone.tab gives Croatia. The zone1970.tab header note is dated 15 May 2025.
